title.narrative: Nutrition Smart Community: Up Scaling the multisectoral approach towards ‘One Planet - Zero Hunger’ Malawi

description.narrative: Overall objective: Contribute to "Zero Hunger" (SDG 2 and the Global Nutrition Targets 2025) in three African countries - Ethiopia, Malawi and Sierra Leone.Project Goal: 9,750 households in the selected vulnerable rural communities apply methods to diversify their food consumption and reduce the prevalence of gastrointestinal infections.Sub-Goal1:7,200 households in the target communities have improved their access to diversified food.Sub-Goal 2: 3,412 households in the target communities improved their practices in nutrition, maternal & childcare, infant feeding, hygiene and health.Sub-Goal 3: 192 Target communities are empowered to develop and manage solutions that contribute to improved nutrition.Sub-Goal 4: Nutrition coordination mechanisms are established and/or strengthened at micro and meso-level and the global NSC has been scaled up and strengthened.

The Nutrition Smart CommUNITY approach encompasses a combination of ‘systemic interventions’ at different level, designed to shift underlying causes of chronic hunger and malnutrition. It is based on 4 strategies: (1) Foster behavior change at household level; (2) Strengthen and support community-based institutions; (3) Activate and improve nutrition relevant services at community level; and (4) Advocate and promote a multisectoral community-based implementation model for the Right to Food. Each community must identify the specific drivers of malnutrition and address the problems using their own existing resources, including government services. The NSC concept combines 5 best practices, namely LANN+ through Participatory Learning and Action, Nutrition Camps, Nutrition Sensitive Agriculture, Nutrition Sensitive Microplanning and Strengthening Institutions.

The planned project covers the entire population of the 192 target villages. 9,750 households will be reached through the interventions, with 57,750 people directly included in the project activities. In Malawi, the total target population in T/A Namkumba is 3,000 households with a total of 16,500 persons (5.5 persons per household). Direct target participants include househoulds with children under the age of five, pregnant and lactating women and farmer households. Particicpants will be reached with project intereventions through health extension workers, agricultural extension workers, care groups and local institutions such as area development committees, village development committes, area nutrition coordinating committees, village nutrition coordinating committees and chiefs.
